newsitem.title: UK: EMU expectations drop in latest week - JP Morgan.
newsitem.headline: EMU expectations drop in latest week - JP Morgan.

text.p: Expectations of a broad-based start to European monetary union in 1999 eased last week, prices monitored by JP Morgan showed.

Financial prices indicate that the probability assumed by the market of Italy, Spain and Sweden joining Germany and France in the first wave of EMU fell during the week, according to the U.S. investment firm's "EMU calculator."
The probability of Italy starting EMU in 1999 dropped three points to 53 percent, and Spain eased six points to 68 percent. Sweden fell four points to 59 percent this week.
The calculator showed the probability of France and Belgium starting EMU remains 100 percent.
JP Morgan point out there is a reasonable margin of error in overall probability levels of between three and five points.

Elsewhere, expectations of first-wave EMU participation by Portugal dropped seven to 71 percent, while Denmark was also down seven percent to 44. The UK was unchanged at 38 percent and Ireland dropped six to 62.
Finland was the only country showing a rise, to 77 percent from 74 but still down from 82 a month ago.
JP Morgan's EMU calculator is derived from the interest rate swaps market.
The probabilities are derived from the actual swap spread, an in-house assumption of what the spread would be if EMU were not a factor, and the expected spread after EMU participation, which is zero.
